experience.player_does: Start the game with the grid hidden and see adjacent cells meet with no gaps; press F2 to reveal the separated grid aid, then press F2 again to return to the seamless surface.
experience.feels_like: Gridlines off reads as one continuous authored surface. Gridlines on intentionally exposes cell boundaries and spacing for alignment.
experience.camera: The fixed logical viewport, cell pitch, map, and menu behavior remain unchanged.
experience.controls: F2 continues to toggle grid visibility only while the world is active.
experience.not_this: Not a change to the persisted map, palette, cell pitch, or the meaning of the cell.inset design tunable when the grid aid is visible.

design_refs.why: The settled cell grammar distinguishes a continuous surface from a deliberately tiled presentation; this makes the hidden-grid state honor that distinction.
The fixed logical presentation and selected cell pitch remain intact while only the optional boundary treatment changes.

considered_existing.why_not: It already owns cell inset, grid visibility, and cell rectangles, so changing the existing draw path avoids a second rendering mode.
The design already defines cell.inset as the presentation gap; no new design section is needed for this implementation correction.

modules.role: Own the conditional cell presentation for the existing world renderer.
modules.why: The seamless off state is a rendering detail coupled to the existing F2 grid toggle.
modules.boundary_data: Reads the existing typed map and boolean grid state, then draws either inset cells with boundaries or full-cell surfaces.

files.why: Apply cell inset only while gridlines are visible so the default hidden-grid state has no gaps between adjacent cells.

functions.signature: func _draw_map_cell(layer: LevelLayer, column: int, row: int) -> void
functions.why: Choose a full-cell rectangle when the grid is hidden and the existing inset rectangle when it is shown.
